claim: Your project history and commendations live only as flat web pages, so from outside these write-ups look rebuilt by hand each time.
problem: The first clause is verified (static pages). The second clause is an inference about Benaka's internal proposal process presented as an outside observation; nothing in the sources shows how write-ups are assembled.
fix: Reword as an explicit inference, e.g. "...live only as flat pages, which makes past-performance assembly look manual from the outside (our inference)".

claim: You have been building since 1994, mostly for federal clients.
problem: Unlabelled characterisation. The site presents five service sectors (government, commercial, institutional, medical, religious) and a client list that includes commercial and municipal work (NJ/NY/MD agencies, Baltimore Orioles). No federal-versus-other revenue split is published.
fix: Hedge to what is visible: "largely federal clients, going by your published client list".

claim: the contact form has no qualification fields
problem: contact-us.html as retrieved contains no form fields at all; the page only says vendors may contact Benaka "by phone, email, or contact form". The sentence asserts a bare form exists rather than that no structured intake exists.
fix: Say "the only published intake is a phone, fax and email address - there is nowhere to submit qualifications".

claim: Impact: $3,000-$10,000 a year in estimator time on today's rework share (Section 2).
problem: Not reachable from the analysis's own assumptions: 10-20 pursuits x 15-30 h/bid x 15-25% rework x $45-55/h loaded gives about $1,000-$8,250, so the $10,000 top exceeds its basis. It also contradicts analysis.json, which states $10,000-$30,000 for the same item.
fix: Use $3,000-$8,000, or state the assumption (e.g. 20 pursuits at 30 h/bid) that justifies $10,000, and reconcile the figure with analysis.json before sending.

claim: Footnote: loaded hourly costs in the impact math are NJ wage data grossed up for benefits and overhead.
problem: Not reproducible for Section 1. The cited O*NET/BLS page gives a NJ construction-manager median of $138,230 (about $66/h); a 25-35% burden gives roughly $83-$90/h, not the ~$55-$70/h implied by 6-10 h/week x 45 weeks = $12,000-$30,000. Direction of error is conservative (range is understated, not inflated), but the arithmetic does not follow from the cited URL.
fix: State the basis as the posted $100K-$140K QC salary band plus 25-35% burden, or recompute the range from the NJ median ($22,000-$40,000) so the footnote and the number agree.

claim: You pursue an Air Force MACC, a Corps MATOC and JOC/IDIQ work.
problem: Present tense is loose. Benaka already holds an Air Force MACC IDIQ (FA448420D0005; successor FA448425D0009 runs to 2032) and was added to the USACE New England small-business MATOC pool in the award disclosed 27 Sep 2026 - it is bidding task orders under them, not still chasing the vehicles.
fix: Reword: "You bid task orders under an Air Force MACC and a Corps small-business MATOC, and hold JOC/IDIQ work."

claim: an Air Force IDIQ at Joint Base McGuire-Dix-Lakehurst
problem: True on the record but not literally supported by the cited URL: the FPDS entry shows Air Force contracting office "FA4484 87 CONS PK" and a place of performance of ZIP 08641, Burlington County, NJ - it never prints the installation name.
fix: Either add a source that names JBMDL, or write "an Air Force MACC run out of the 87th Contracting Squadron in New Jersey".

problem: Body (headline through the disclaimer, excluding "For the founder" and Sources) is about 445 words, and about 460 if slash/hyphenated compounds are counted as separate words - at or marginally over the ceiling with no margin.
fix: Cut ~30 words, e.g. trim the section headings and the "Why this works" bullets, to land near 410-420.
